## Overview

The Jade Wardens are the eastern barbarian tribe of Kythoria, inhabiting regions dominated by forests, rivers, and mist-covered valleys. Unlike the other tribes, the relative peace of the eastern region has allowed the Jade Wardens to cultivate something the other orders rarely have the luxury of pursuing: time — time to study, train, understand, and prepare. They serve as the eastern frontier order, protecting civilization from the monstrous lands beyond.

---

## Territory

The Jade Wardens inhabit the eastern regions of Kythoria, a land dominated by forests, rivers, and mist-covered valleys. Their main settlement is built around a great valley, with smaller villages, training grounds, and watch posts scattered throughout the surrounding territory. Rather than one enormous fortress, their territory is interconnected by temples, monasteries, fortified villages, and secluded training grounds. The central settlement serves as both the political and spiritual heart of the tribe. It is here that the great masters teach, warriors train, scholars conduct their studies, and important decisions concerning the eastern frontier are made.

---

## Culture

The culture of the Jade Wardens is built around the belief that true strength begins within. They have developed a culture centered around discipline, self-mastery, and understanding. A warrior is expected to develop both body and mind. Physical training is only one part of their education. Meditation, philosophy, spiritual studies, history, monster anatomy, and the study of supernatural forces are all considered valuable forms of knowledge.

Their temples and training halls often serve multiple purposes: a place of meditation can also be a library; a monastery can contain a training ground; a scholar may also be a warrior, and a warrior may eventually become a teacher. Knowledge is not considered separate from combat — knowledge is what allows combat to become mastery.

---

## Philosophy

The Jade Wardens believe that uncontrolled strength is ultimately weakness. A warrior who cannot control their fear, anger, pride, or desire is considered vulnerable regardless of how powerful they may be. Their philosophy revolves around balance: body and spirit, strength and restraint, knowledge and action, life and death.

The Wardens do not seek to eliminate emotion. Instead, they believe emotion must be understood before it can be mastered. This philosophy extends to their study of monsters. Rather than seeing every supernatural creature as nothing more than an enemy, the Wardens seek to understand what a creature is, why it behaves as it does, and what forces shape it. They believe understanding an enemy does not mean sympathizing with it — it means becoming capable of defeating it.

Their philosophy could be summarized as: *"A blade without discipline is no different from the beast it seeks to kill."*

---

## The Way of the Spirit

One of the defining characteristics of the Jade Wardens is their study of the spirit. For generations, their monks, scholars, and mystics have studied questions that other tribes rarely have the time or inclination to investigate: what separates body from soul, what remains after death, what allows supernatural beings to persist beyond the destruction of their bodies, can the spirit be strengthened.

Their studies are not necessarily considered forbidden — they are simply dangerous. The Wardens maintain strict traditions concerning what knowledge may be pursued and how it may be used. This has created a culture in which spiritual disciplines are considered an essential part of understanding the supernatural world.

---

## The Emerald Path

The Jade Wardens have their own rite through which an apprentice becomes a full Warden. The candidate must face a challenge specifically designed to expose their greatest weakness: fear, anger, pride, doubt, attachment. The exact challenge differs between individuals. The purpose is not necessarily to overcome the weakness completely, but to recognize it. A Warden who understands their weakness can control it. A Warden who refuses to acknowledge it will eventually be controlled by it.

---

## Attitude

Jade Wardens tend to be disciplined, patient, reserved, observant, respectful, introspective, highly traditional, and slow to act without understanding the situation. They generally avoid unnecessary confrontation. A Warden does not rush into battle simply because an enemy appears — they observe, assess, prepare, and then strike. This can sometimes cause friction with the other tribes, particularly warriors who believe hesitation gives monsters time to grow stronger.

- Monk
- Fighter

- Rogue

- Wizard

---

## Weapons & Equipment

Jade Wardens' equipment emphasizes precision, balance, and craftsmanship. Their arsenal includes curved swords, polearms, bows, short blades, spears, staves, and specialized weapons designed around particular martial disciplines. Their equipment often incorporates jade, lacquered wood, silk, engraved metal, and other materials associated with their culture. Weapons are not merely tools — a warrior is expected to develop a relationship with their weapon through years of practice. A master may use the same weapon for decades.

---

## Relationship with Monsters

The Jade Wardens possess perhaps the most academic approach to monsters among the four tribes. They maintain extensive records concerning supernatural creatures, documenting behavior, anatomy, weaknesses, origins, magical properties, spiritual characteristics, and historical encounters. Some creatures have been studied for generations.

This knowledge is shared carefully with the other tribes when necessary. The Jade Wardens believe that every encounter with a monster is an opportunity to learn something that may save lives in the future. Their libraries therefore contain centuries of accumulated knowledge.
